style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: 200mm telephoto compression of a warehouse aisle: floor-to-ceiling racking in corrugated steel, some polymer bins bulging with parts while adjacent bins sit nearly empty, low raking daylight from the right cutting long shadows across concrete, graphite, cobalt blue and safety yellow accents, deep industrial contrast, asymmetric vertical layers stacked by lens compression, no people, no text, fine film grain.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, watermarks, logos, UI
rationale: This is a systemic inventory-buffer misallocation story best shown through physical racking scale. Telephoto compression stacks the racking layers to reveal the uneven stocking without abstract shapes, and the warehouse aisle fits the publication's industrial world.
cue: a blanket 98% keeps about 2.5 times the buffer
subject: warehouse racking bins unequally stocked, some overflowing, others near-empty
core_thesis: A blanket 98% fill target over-funds margin-rich items by about 2.5 times their defensible buffer while holding barely half the buffer a cheap line-stopping part justifies.
core_conflict: uniform service-level target vs item-specific miss/carry cost ratio
composition: asymmetric vertical racking layers compressed by telephoto, hero off-center

title: 98% Fill Target Hides Four Sigma

review.depicts: A long, telephoto-compressed aisle between tall orange-and-grey steel racking units filled with blue plastic bins of small metal hardware, with yellow protective posts at the rack bases and daylight falling in bands down the concrete floor.
review.reason: It shows warehouse racking bins of small parts with visibly uneven fill levels, which is the physical form of the buffer and fill-target mechanism the article argues about, though the stocking variance is subtle rather than dramatically lopsided.
